input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI stripping applies, the prompt text is passed through .strip(), which removes the trailing space before the input cursor and any leading whitespace from the prompt.
- rationale: Trigger: click.prompt() on a non-TTY stream (so should_strip_ansi is true) with a prompt whose suffix is ': '. The prompt text becomes 'Name:' instead of 'Name: ', so the user's typed input is shown directly after the colon. Impact: the prompt output differs from the unstripped path and from the TTY path, with no space before the cursor, a visible regression in piped or captured prompt output.
critique: The finding names the same operation: .strip() applied after ANSI stripping removes the trailing space from 'Name: '. It also gives the same trigger (non-TTY, should_strip_ansi true) and the same consequence, a prompt that differs from the TTY path.
